definition: Vehemently means marked by intense force or emotion.
task: Write one sentence of your own using the word vehemently. Make the sentence show what the word means -- a reader who did not know vehemently should be able to work it out from your sentence.
avoid_verbatim: The twins opposed selling the lake cottage vehemently, itemizing forty summers of reasons before the realtor had finished her coffee.
Insistently keeps returning to the point and won't drop it; vehemently adds the force of real feeling to the asking.
Furiously goes past vehemently — the force has become anger outright, and the argument is now a fight.

Fiercely is intensity with open ferocity in it — teeth showing, an edge of attack in the voice or the eyes. Vehemently is intense feeling driving the words, and it can stay perfectly controlled, even quiet. A fierce denial snarls; a vehement one can be nearly whispered and still burn.

Forcefully means with strength — weight and momentum behind the words — but not necessarily with feeling; a lawyer can argue forcefully about a clause she cares nothing for. Vehemently requires the feeling: the intensity comes from emotion, and the force is the heat escaping.
with the heat turned all the way down
with too little feeling to matter

Latin vehemens may be from vehere, 'to carry' (carried away by feeling), or from ve- + mens, 'out of one's mind' — Roman grammarians themselves disagreed, and no other English word grew from either branch through this one. Some words arrive whole; this one arrived at full volume.

The idea seemed harmless: brighten the chapel's faded fresco with a modern glaze.
The restorer's answer was not harmless.
She objected vehemently — voice low and shaking, a folder of pigment analyses laid out page by page, and her resignation, signed and dated, drawn from her bag in case the point was unclear.
Vehemently is the exact word because it names expression driven by intense force and feeling.
She isn't merely firm — firm doesn't bring a resignation letter.
The intensity is the information: whatever she is saying, the force with which she says it has become part of the message.
Vehemently turns the intensity dial on a verb of speech or stance — deny, object, oppose, insist.
The force is feeling, not volume: a vehement refusal can be nearly whispered, which is exactly where it parts company with this unit's vociferous, the word for loudness itself.
If the feeling is everyday and only the grip is tight, firmly is the honest adverb.
